name: MILO
description: Milo is a partnership domino game played in Africa and parts of Indonesia. It uses the same equipment and basic play as Latin Partnership Dominoes, but with different scoring: the winning partnership gets one point for domino; if blocked, the partnership with the smallest total of pips on their tiles gets one point; if the tile that made domino causes both ends of the train to end in the same suit, the partnership scores two points (called a Milo). A game is five points.

Country/Region of Origin: Africa and parts of Indonesia
Time Period: Not specified
Historical Development: Milo is a scoring variant of Latin Partnership Dominoes, popular in Spain and Latin America; the Milo variant is played under this name in Africa and Indonesia.
Cultural Significance: Social and family partnership game.
Four players in fixed partnerships. Partners sit facing each other.

Type: Double-six domino set
Number of tiles: 28
All tiles dealt to the four players.

Double-six domino set (28 tiles)
Table space
All 28 tiles are dealt; seven tiles each. Play is normally counter-clockwise.
